### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A14, A15 and A20 each appeared in about 47 in 100 traces (94 of 200); in the later window, each appears in about 99–100 in 100 traces (199 of 200), still at most once per trace in both windows. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- A36, which occurs in every trace in both windows, was followed by A14 in about 47 in 100 of its outgoing transitions earlier and by A21 in about 53 in 100; in the later window, about 99.5 in 100 of its outgoing transitions go to A14 and only about 0.5 in 100 to A21. [DIR001]
- The three activities, which earlier appeared together in about 47 in 100 traces and were jointly absent in about 53 in 100, now co-occur in about 99.5 in 100 traces in a fixed order: A14 before A20 before A15. [REL001, REL002, REL007]
- The block sits between A36 and A21: in the later window, A36 precedes each of the three and each of the three precedes A21 in about 99.5 in 100 traces, whereas earlier A21 usually ran without the block (about 53 in 100 traces). [REL003, REL004, REL008, REL009, REL012, REL013]
- Relations around the block adjusted accordingly: A37, earlier without A14 in about 53 in 100 traces, now co-occurs with it in about 99.5 in 100 (A14 first in about 54 in 100, interleaved in about 46 in 100), and A40 no longer appears without A14 (about 33 in 100 traces earlier, none later) although A40's own frequency is roughly stable at about 60–62 in 100. [REL005, REL006, REL010, REL011, REL014, REL015]
- Small positional shifts accompany this: A21's mean relative position moved slightly later (about 0.41 to 0.43) and A36's slightly earlier (about 0.33 to 0.30). [POS001, POS002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the activity block A14 → A20 → A15, executed between A36 and A21, changed from optional to essentially mandatory: in the earlier window it ran in about 47 in 100 cases and was skipped in the rest, with A36 passing directly to A21 in about 53 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, while in the later window it runs in about 99–100 in 100 cases and the direct A36-to-A21 route has practically disappeared. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001]

The support is direct and consistent: all three participation items show the same rise without any change in repetition, the successor profile of A36 flipped from roughly half A14 and half A21 to almost exclusively A14, and the relational items show the three activities now always co-occurring in a fixed order before A21. Many items reflect the same underlying trace behaviour, but the screening found 21 qualifying items against fewer than 1 expected by chance in this family, so the pattern as a whole is not what an unchanged process typically produces. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, REL001, REL002, REL007, REL003, REL008, REL012]

An important competing explanation remains: the two windows may simply sample different mixes of cases (for example, mostly block-executing case types after the change point) rather than reflecting a changed routing rule, and the evidence contains no time or resource items, so timing and allocation are not addressed. [OCC001, DIR001]

Other differences: A21's mean relative position shifted slightly later (about 0.41 to 0.43) and A36's slightly earlier (about 0.33 to 0.30), and the relations of A37 and A40 to the block changed as described above; since both activities' own frequencies are stable, these look like side effects of the block becoming mandatory rather than independent changes. [POS001, POS002, REL005, REL006, REL010, REL011, REL014, REL015]
